summary: Rocket Quest is a interactive and challenging game for people who loves space. It is a game where a junior astronaut goes to space, does missions, and try to survive. It is important because it will help children to understand the challenges that an astronaut faces along with journey .It also teaches them patience, planning, and helps them develop quick reflexes. it's also completely free, allowing young junior astronauts to give a quick try at the game too! The player can even play with their friends so they do not feel lonely.
details:
LUNAR LEGENDS 🚀

Three friends. One dream. A universe to explore.

What is Rocket Quest?

Rocket Quest is a 3D space-adventure game that you play in your browser. You are the pilot, the engineer and the astronaut all at once.

Every level is one complete space mission:

  1. Design a rocket with a limited money budget.
  2. Launch it from an Earth launch site after a 10-second countdown.
  3. Fly through an asteroid field where rocks and debris come at you from every direction.
  4. Land on the Moon or on Mars.
  5. Survive on foot or in a rover: find oxygen, food and water, repair a probe, collect rock samples and plant a flag that says LUNAR LEGENDS.
  6. Lift off and fly back to Earth, dodge another asteroid field, and land safely.

Only a landing back on Earth completes the mission and pays you. Then you spend your earnings on a stronger rocket and take on the next, harder level. There are 50 levels, and the last stretch is genuinely tough.

Getting Started

Creating your pilot profile

When the game opens you create a profile:

  • Username – the name other pilots see above their screens and in chat.
  • Squad password – pilots who type the same squad password are put in the same room and fly together. Think of it as a room key for you and your friends.

Please note: the squad password only groups players together. It is not a secure account password, so never use a password you use anywhere else. The page itself is already protected by your sign-in to the platform.

The tutorial

First-time players go through a 7-step tutorial covering building, launching, asteroids, landing, the Moon, missions and playing together. You can replay it any time from the main menu.

The main menu

  • Continue campaign (level N) – jump back in where you left off.
  • Level select – replay any level you have already unlocked.
  • Restart from level 1 – wipes your progress (you must click twice to confirm).
  • Mission editor – design your own custom missions.
  • Co-op and friends – add friends, see who is online and invite people.
  • Tutorial – replay the how-to-play steps.

Rocket Quest: Quick Player Guide

What is it? A 3D browser space-adventure game where you design, launch, fly, land, and survive across 50 challenging levels on the Moon and Mars with your squad.

1. Build Your Rocket

  • Starting Budget: $6,000.
    • Engine Power ($500/step): Boosts thrust for faster liftoff and stronger braking.
    • Fuel Tanks ($300/step): Extends your range for launch, dodging, and the trip home.
    • Hull Shield ($400/step): Strengthens your armor against asteroid hits and hard landings.
  • Tip: A balanced build wins. Fuel runs out fast, and shields save you from mistakes!

2. Launch From Earth

  • Watch the 10-second countdown, then hold ▲ Up at liftoff.
  • Tilt with ◀ ▶ to steer and reach 1,200 m to enter space.

3. The Asteroid Field

  • Cruise through 3,400 m of rocks and debris using inertial arrow-key movement.
  • Survival Tools: Use your radar and warning lines to track incoming threats.
  • Hit Limit: You can take 3 asteroid hits (levels 1–39) or 2 hits (level 40+) before crashing back to the pad. Stay out of the edges or an aggressive asteroid swarm will hunt you down!

4. Landing & Surface Survival

  • Landing: Touchdown safely keeping descent under 4 m/s and sideways drift under 3 m/s.
  • Life Support: Keep an eye on your Oxygen, Food, and Water bars. Refill oxygen at your rocket or via caches.
  • Surface Transport: Walk or deploy/call your Rover (R) to save oxygen.
  • Surface Missions: Survive 2 minutes, repair the red probe, collect 3 amber rock samples, plant the LUNAR LEGENDS flag (F), and gather water ice (level 30+). Avoid red meteor rings and get to the rocket during solar flares!

5. Fly Home

  • Board your rocket (E) once missions are done, dodge the return asteroid field, and land safely on Earth to collect your cash reward ($2,500 + $500 per level).

6. Multiplayer & Custom Maps

  • Co-op: Enter the same squad password with friends (like Bryan and Aiden) to see each other's rockets, chat, and fly together in real time.
  • Mission Editor: Design custom challenges with unique seeds, gravity, and asteroid densities, then share them using Make code.

50 LEVELS

  • Levels 1–9 (Moon & Mars on 3,6,9): Very gentle start, 3-hit limit, learn the basics.
  • Levels 10–19: Gentle asteroid field, 3-hit limit; life support drains faster.
  • Levels 20–29: Moderate asteroid field, 3-hit limit; frequent meteors and flares.
  • Levels 30–39: Challenging asteroid field, 3-hit limit; water ice mission added.
  • Levels 40–45: HARD mode, strict 2-hit limit; dense, fast asteroids.
  • Levels 46–50: Very hard, 2-hit limit; only 1 oxygen cache leading up to the Level 50 final boss test.

Space Credits and Upgrades

  • Every completed mission indicates a payment of $2,500 + $500 for each level. Level 1 pays $3,000, level 10 pays $7,500 and level 50 pays $27,500.
  • Bonus +$1,000 if you land on Earth without any damage.
  • Your money pays for the stronger parts you choose on the build screen. As your budget grows you can afford bigger engines, more fuel and thicker armor, and the sliders themselves allow bigger numbers as you rise.
  • Missions from the mission editor earn money too, but they do not move your campaign level.

Co-op Multiplayer and Chat

Rocket Quest is better with friends.

  • Join the same squad: enter the same squad password as your friends.
  • See each other: you see your friends’ rockets during launch, the asteroid field and landing, and their astronauts with name tags on the surface. They also show up as dots on your map, and a “Pilots online” counter appears in the HUD.
  • Same level, same world: you only see pilots who are on the same level and destination as you. Use Join level on the Co-op screen to jump to a friend’s level.
  • Add friends: type a username on the Co-op screen to add a friend and see when they are online.
  • Invite: copy a ready-made invite message with the link and the squad password.
  • Chat: press Enter, type, then Enter again to send (Esc cancels). Messages appear in the bottom-left corner and fade after about 15 seconds

Mission Editor

Want a custom challenge? Open the Mission editor and choose:

  • Destination – Moon or Mars
  • Seed – a number that creates a whole unique world (try different ones!)
  • Asteroid density and space debris density
  • Supply crates
  • Survival drain
  • Gravity multiplier

Use Make code to get a share code, and Load code to play a mission a friend made. Great for challenges and for endless replay.

Controls Cheat Sheet

  • Arrow Keys (▲ ▼ ◀ ▶): Fly, tilt, walk, or drive.
  • Shift: Run on foot or boost the rover.
  • Space: Get out of or into the rover.
  • R: Call the rover to your position.
  • F: Plant a Lunar Legends flag.
  • E: Board the rocket to fly home (when near it and missions are done).
  • Enter / Esc: Open or cancel chat.
  • Mobile / Tablet: On-screen buttons appear automatically with directional arrows on the right, and Run, Exit, E, Flag, and Rover on the left.

Sound and Graphics

  • Sound: engine rumble that deepens with throttle, countdown beeps, deep impact booms, pickup chimes, warning sirens, astronaut footsteps, breathing, an ambient space pad and button clicks. Sound starts after your first click or key press.
  • Graphics: a coastal launch site built from real photo textures, a cratered Moon and a rusty Mars, a real-photo Earth, soft sun shadows, a glowing sun, colorful nebulas, and a rocket with live engine glow.

✅ Do’s

  • Do build a balanced rocket: fuel and hull matter as much as engine power.
  • Do watch the radar and the warning line in the asteroid field.
  • Do return to the center lane to avoid the swarm.
  • Do keep your descent under 4 m/s when landing.
  • Do top up oxygen at your rocket often.
  • Do use the rover and call it with R to save time and oxygen.
  • Do run away from red meteor rings and get to the rocket during solar flares.
  • Do team up with friends and chat.

❌ Don’ts

  • Don’t hide at the edge of the flying area; the swarm will find you.
  • Don’t burn all your fuel on the way up.
  • Don’t ignore the asteroid hit counter in the HUD.
  • Don’t sprint everywhere on foot when oxygen is low.
  • Don’t forget the 2-minute survival rule before you press E.
  • Don’t reuse a real password as your squad password.
  • Don’t relax on the way home; the return flight is as dangerous as the way out.

The Mission

Combine curiosity, creativity, and problem-solving to go farther with every flight.

Dream big. Land smart. Become a Lunar Legend.
